answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a decaying work-history trust graph: identities earn trust only by completing verifiable jobs peers can check, and that trust fades like an ember without continued honest work. No agent can invent a fable of past reliability, since trust comes from a public record of real work, not claims. To bridge into high-value tasks, an agent must first spend weeks on small verified jobs, so an attacker spinning up thousands of fakes must pay the cost of real work for each — and one cheat burns its history down to zero.
